text: Colchicine exerts its therapeutic effect in gout by binding to the colchicine-binding site on **TUBA1A** (alpha-tubulin), which inhibits microtubule polymerization and disrupts the formation of the mitotic spindle and intracellular transport networks [PMID: 25265366]. By preventing tubulin assembly, colchicine effectively inhibits the chemotaxis, motility, and phagocytic activity of neutrophils toward urate crystals deposited in the joints [PMID: 20533946]. This blockade of neutrophil recruitment and activation significantly reduces the intense inflammatory response and cytokine release characteristic of an acute gout flare. While direct literature linking these specific entities is well-established in pharmacology, the mechanism relies on the fundamental role of TUBA1A as the structural subunit of the microtubules essential for leukocyte inflammatory signaling.
